findings.observation: GW-EVIDENCE-01 is not enforced. src/evidence/verify.ts:47-50 and src/evidence/verify.ts:119-171 define a SHA-matching caller-authored list of {id,status} values as raw execution; the candidate artifact .delivery/tasks/global-workflow-repair/artifacts/evidence-validation.json:1-15 is exactly such a handwritten PASS list and contains neither environment identity nor observed command output. src/evidence/verify.ts:198-200 and src/evidence/verify.ts:251-258 compare commits but discard the recorded tree fields, while src/commands/task-verify.ts:178-181 verifies only whatever non-empty Git-identity subset the caller supplies. Fresh adversarial review retained valid:true after changing the EngineeringGovernance evidence tree to forty f characters and after reducing Git verification from five repositories to one. The real executions and the claimed absence of Simulator, device, runtime, or external mutation therefore cannot be independently established.

GW-EXIT-01 and GW-PILOT-01 do not fail closed across review and closure. src/commands/task-review.ts:4-22 accepts only caller-supplied owner strings and blocking IDs; it does not load a review artifact, contract digest, candidate identities, finding classifications, or prior candidate decision. src/commands/task-close.ts:8-20 trusts caller-supplied state:ACCEPTED, projectStatusValid, and pending IDs, and src/cli/main.ts:102-110 exposes those artifact-free decisions directly. Fresh real-CLI checks returned exit 0 and valid:true for an arbitrary distinct R3 reviewer with no candidate and for a close request with no contract, evidence, or review. Incomplete evidence can therefore advance, and exact independent R2/R3 acceptance is not enforced.

GW-ADOPT-01 does not cover the ProjTrav three-repository generated-target boundary. src/project/adoption-profile.ts:74-81 declares the server and iOS generated targets, but src/commands/adopt.ts:323-350 includes only adapter sources in the overlap guard and planned writes. tests/integration/real-project-dry-run.test.ts:37-47 likewise snapshots no projtrav-server or projtrav-ios generated target. A fresh ProjTrav-shaped repository with a dirty projtrav-server/AGENTS.md still produced a successful plan containing only root .delivery files and Docs rule sources, with no generated target operation. The frozen observation that three-repository targets are planned and overlapping dirty paths stop before writes is therefore not met; a later native sync can overwrite an unguarded concurrent target edit.

The portable project gate reports compliance on an unsupported Node runtime. package.json:6-8 restricts the runner to Node 22, but templates/ci/check-delivery-policy.sh:67-70 invokes ambient npm and node without selecting or validating that runtime. A fresh pinned-policy check under the shell's Node 25.9.0 emitted npm EBADENGINE and then returned valid:true. The global launcher does prefer /opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin, but the portable gate does not, weakening clean-machine reproducibility and allowing runtime drift to pass silently.

nextStage: REPAIR_REQUIRED -> IN_PROGRESS under the existing implementation owner codex. Repair the same frozen contract across the evidence/Git trust boundary, artifact-bound review and closure chain, ProjTrav generated-target planning and overlap guard, and portable Node runtime gate; regenerate fresh machine-derived evidence and exact candidate identities, then obtain a new independent R3 review before merge or any real global installation.
